text:
maria: Hey team — opened my first PR for the auth-messaging feature, curious about the preferred flow here. I pushed branch feat/PLAT-842-auth-messaging and the PR is in draft. What do y'all expect for commit messages, and should I squash before marking ready?

sam: Welcome aboard, maria! :tada: Our usual is a single logical commit per PR for small changes, but if you need history keep commits and add a final squash before merge. For commit message format use: 

```
<scope>(<area>): <short summary>\\n\\nA short body describing motivation and key changes.\\n
Refs: PLAT-842
```

(So e.g., "auth(messaging): add outbound queue for notification events")

leo: Also, branch naming looks good. For bigger features we accept multiple commits while iterating; mark the PR Ready for Review by removing the draft toggle and add the label needs-review. CODEOWNERS will auto-request reviewers.

maria: Thanks — do we have any pre-commit hooks / linters I should run locally? I ran a quick `make test` but saw a few formatting failures.

sam: Yep, run `pre-commit install` then `pre-commit run --all-files`. We use ruff for linting and black for formatting. `make dev` spins up the local server (and migrations). If you hit type errors run `poetry run ruff` or `make typecheck`.

leo: CI jobs to watch: ci/unit-tests, ci/typecheck, ci/integration. If ci/unit-tests flakes, add the label flaky-ci and ping #eng-sre.

maria: Good to know. One more: what's our rebase vs merge policy? I rebased on main earlier and had to resolve conflicts. Should I rebase before merging?

sam: We prefer a clean history on main. Rebase your branch onto origin/main and force-push (`git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main && git push --force-with-lease`) if the PR is marked draft. If it's already under review avoid force-pushes unless requested. For small fixes, squash+merge from the UI is common.

leo: If you're touching infra or deployment manifests add the label eng-approval and mention @sam for signoff. Also, if you need backports to stable release branches, add the label needs-backport and include the target branch in the PR description.

maria: Got it. What about reviewer etiquette? Any checklist I should attach to the PR?

sam: Short checklist in the PR body is helpful:
- What changed and why (1-2 short bullets)
- How to test locally (commands)
- Any risk / perf impact
- Migration notes (if any)

Example: 
```
What: add outbound queue for auth notification events
How: run `make dev` and POST to /api/test-notify, see queue items in redis
Risk: small, logging only; no schema changes
Backport: none
```

leo: Also include the ticket link at top (PLAT-842). If CI is green and reviewers LGTM, we usually merge within 1 business day. If you need a faster turnaround add `urgent` label and ping me or the on-call reviewer.

devex-bot: quick tip — to request a fresh review after updates add the comment: `@repo-bot request-review` (this triggers the request-review workflow).

maria: One tiny practical: I had to re-run `pre-commit` on a separate file and the hook changed a lot of whitespace. Is that expected?

sam: Pre-commit should be deterministic. If it reformats many files, run `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and include those formatting changes in your PR. Try `git reset --soft origin/main && git commit -m "chore(format): apply black/ruff"` to bundle formatting as a separate commit if needed.

leo: And if you want, mark the PR draft as "ready for review" only after you run the suite locally and the formatting/linting are fixed. Otherwise reviewers will ask for those first.

maria: Perfect, super helpful. I'll tidy this up and ping when it's ready. Thanks! :pray:

ci-bot: ci/unit-tests started — 12 tasks queued.

sam: welcome again! ping me if you get stuck with the rebase conflicts, happy to pair for a few minutes.

maria: Will do — thanks everyone :)
